newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA EXTENDS 2ND INNINGS LEAD VS INDIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA EXTENDS 2ND INNINGS LEAD VS INDIA.

text.p: South Africa, who took a stranglehold on the first test after routing India for a paltry 100 at Kingsmead on Friday, opened up a 166-run lead by tea on the second day.
Although left-handed opener Gary Kirsten was dismissed cheaply for two for the second time in the match, South Africa reached tea on 31 for one in their second innings.
South Africa's first innings top-scorer Andrew Hudson was unbeaten on 19 and his partner Adam Bacher four not out.
But the day's first two sessions were dominated by the South African fast bowlers who took full advantage of a pitch offering both pace and bounce to bowl India out for 100 in just 39.1 overs.

India's total was the third lowest at test level ever compiled at Kingsmead after Australia's 75 and South Africa's 99 in the same match during the 1949-50 series. It was also India's lowest test total posted against South Africa.
Allan Donald, the spearhead of the South African attack, took 5-40 - his seventh five-wicket haul at test level - while Shaun Pollock returned figures of 2-18 and all-rounder Brian McMillan 2-27.
No Indian batsman reached 20 and their lower order collapsed tamely after lunch to lose five wickets in 12.1 overs - three of them departing off successive deliveries.
In the third over after lunch, McMillan captured the wicket of Rahul Dravid who, playing defensively from the crease, was given out leg before wicket for seven.

Donald then claimed two more wickets with the next two balls. Mongia edged Donald through to wicketkeeper Dave Richardson on four and Javagal Srinath, trying to fend off a lifting delivery, was brilliantly caught by a diving Daryll Cullinan from firstslip.

Four overs later, David Johnson was unfortunate to be given out by New Zealand umpire Steve Dunne. Another rearing Donald bumper struck Johnson on the shoulder as he took evasive action but he was given out caught at short leg by Bacher for three.
